summary: mojolint — pattern lints for the origin and thread-safety mistakes the Mojo compiler accepts. Text-only by default; with `--lsp`, the rules ask `mojo-lsp-server` for resolved types and name-resolved uses. A proof of concept; see the README.

modules.summary: mojolint — pattern lints for the origin and thread-safety mistakes the Mojo compiler accepts. Text-only by default; with `--lsp`, the rules ask `mojo-lsp-server` for resolved types and name-resolved uses. A proof of concept; see the README.
What the compiler knows and the text does not, fetched in one LSP batch.
modules.description:
For every function: its resolved signature. For every `var` local: its
resolved type and every name-resolved use. For every struct field: its
resolved type. That is the whole of what the rules ask the compiler for, and
it is enough to replace the three textual guesses in tier 1 — "mentioned
again" (references), "spelled `MutUntrackedOrigin`" (types, so aliases and
helpers count), and "built as `var x = S(`" (types again).

`Facts()` with no arguments is the empty set; every lookup then comes back
empty and the rules fall back to their textual form.

fields.name: errors
fields.summary: Parse errors the server reported: types may be missing when > 0.

fields.name: local_uses
fields.summary: Every reference to a local, declaration first, sorted.

overloads.summary: The resolved type of local `name` in `f`; empty if unknown.

overloads.signature: def last_use(self, f: Func, name: String) -> Optional[Pos]
overloads.summary: The last reference to local `name` after its declaration.

overloads.summary: `def f(...)` with every type resolved; empty if unknown.

overloads.signature: def collect_facts(path: String, source: String, lines: List[Line], mod: Module, include: List[String]) -> Facts
overloads.summary: Ask the server about every function, local and field in `mod`.

modules.summary: A small JSON reader and writer — enough for JSON-RPC.
modules.description:
Parsed documents are arenas: every value is a `JsonNode` in `JsonDoc.nodes`,
children are indices, and the root is node 0. That keeps the type flat (no
recursive struct) and makes lookups cheap: `doc.get(node, "key")`,
`doc.at(node, i)`, `doc.string(node)`, `doc.int(node)`. A missing key or a
type mismatch gives `-1` / an empty value rather than raising, so a chain of
lookups over a reply that may not have the shape we hoped for reads straight.

fields.name: text
fields.summary: The decoded string, the number's spelling, or `true`/`false`.

fields.name: keys
fields.summary: Object keys, parallel to `children`; empty for arrays.

fields.name: children
fields.summary: Indices of array items or object values, in document order.

overloads.signature: def get(self, node: Int, key: String) -> Int
overloads.summary: The value of `key` in object `node`, or -1.

overloads.signature: def at(self, node: Int, index: Int) -> Int
overloads.summary: Item `index` of array `node`, or -1.
Number of items in an array or members in an object; 0 otherwise.
The text of a string node; empty for anything else.

overloads.signature: def int(self, node: Int, default: Int = Int(-1)) -> Int
overloads.summary: The value of an integer number node, else `default`.
Parse one JSON value; the root is node 0.
`text` as a JSON string literal, quotes included.

modules.description:
The server's `--mojo-test` mode reads `// -----`-delimited JSON-RPC messages
from stdin, answers every request before it honours `shutdown`, and runs
single-threaded — a design for scripted use. So the client is a batch: queue
`initialize`, `didOpen`, any number of `hover`/`references` queries, then
`shutdown`/`exit`; write the lot to a file; run the server once with stdin
redirected; parse the `Content-Length`-framed replies and index them by id.
No pipes, no threads, one process per file, well under a second with `std`
loaded.

Positions are LSP positions: 0-based line, 0-based UTF-16 column. The linter
works in bytes and 1-based lines; `Pos` converts at the boundary and the
column difference only matters after a non-ASCII character on the same line.

structs.name: Pos
structs.summary: A 1-based line and 0-based byte column, as the linter counts.

structs.name: LspBatch
structs.summary: The requests for one document, in order.

fields.name: body
fields.summary: The delimited request stream, without the closing shutdown/exit.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, path: String, source: String)
def hover(mut self, at: Pos) -> Int
overloads.summary: Queue a hover at `at`; returns the request id.

overloads.signature: def references(mut self, at: Pos) -> Int
overloads.summary: Queue a references query (declaration included) at `at`.
Run the server over the queued requests and collect its replies.

structs.name: LspReplies
structs.summary: Every message the server sent, parsed, with requests indexed by id.

fields.name: ids
fields.summary: `ids[k]` is the id of `docs[k]`, or -1 for a notification.

fields.name: errors
fields.summary: Diagnostics of severity 1 (error) the server published.

overloads.summary: The first line of the hover's code block: `(variable) var t: T`, `(argument) p: T`, `(field) var cell: T`, `(function) def f(...)`. Empty when the server had nothing to say.
The start of every location in a references reply, sorted.
The bodies of the `Content-Length:`-framed messages in `stream`.
The type in a hover line: everything after the first `: ` of `(variable) var t: Pointer[T, MutUntrackedOrigin]`; empty if none.
The `def ...` of a `(function) def f(...)` hover line; empty if none.

modules.summary: The rules. Each is one function over a file's logical lines and its recovered structure, returning `Finding`s. `RULES` is the table the CLI and the corpus harness read; add an entry and a branch in `run_rule` for L004.

overloads.summary: Every rule, in the order they run.

overloads.signature: def check_l001(path: String, lines: List[Line], mod: Module, facts: Facts) -> List[Finding]
overloads.summary: `Pointer(to=x)` erased to an untracked or opaque pointer, where either
overloads.description:
- the line is a `return`: the untracked pointer leaves the function while
  `x` (a parameter or local) does not; or
- `x` is a `var` local of this function and is never mentioned again:
  Mojo destroys `x` at that last use, before anything reads the pointer.

An erased pointer passed as an argument to a call, from a parameter, is
fine — a parameter is alive for the whole call, joins included — which is
how the library's own typed `parallel_for` looks, and why it is silent.

With facts, the second case is decided by the compiler: the last
name-resolved use of `x`, and whether the line binds a value whose
resolved type is an untracked pointer or a struct wrapping one — so
`var ctx = Ctx.to(x)` is caught at the call, not inside the helper.

overloads.signature: def check_l002(path: String, lines: List[Line], mod: Module, facts: Facts) -> List[Finding]
overloads.summary: A struct with `__deinit__`/`__del__` and an untracked pointer field, dereferenced as `local.field[]` from outside its methods.
overloads.description:
`local.field[]` copies the pointer out and, if that is `local`'s last
use, the destructor runs between the copy and the deref. A method borrows
the whole struct for the call; so does `OwnedPointer.__getitem__`.

With facts, the field's type is the resolved one, the owners are every
local whose resolved type is the struct (however it was built), and the
deref must sit on the owner's last use.

overloads.signature: def check_l003(path: String, lines: List[Line], mod: Module, facts: Facts) -> List[Finding]
overloads.summary: A plain store to shared state inside a task-shaped function.
overloads.description:
Fires on `t.field = …` (typed shape) and `p[].field = …` (any shape). A
subscripted target such as `s.cells[i] = …` is taken to be a per-task
slot and left alone; atomics never appear on the left of `=`.

overloads.signature: def run_rule(id: String, path: String, lines: List[Line], mod: Module, facts: Facts) -> List[Finding]
def lint_source(path: String, source: String) -> List[Finding]
overloads.summary: Every finding for one file, sorted by line — text only, no compiler.

overloads.signature: def lint_with_facts(path: String, source: String, facts: Facts) -> List[Finding]
overloads.summary: Every finding for one file, sorted by line, using `facts` where the rules have a use for them (`collect_facts` fills them from the LSP).

modules.summary: Functions, parameters, structs and fields, recovered from logical lines by indentation alone.
modules.description:
A `def` header at indent *k* owns every following line with indent > *k*;
the same for `struct`. That is enough to know, for any line, which function
it is in and what that function's parameters and `var` locals are called —
the whole vocabulary the rules use.

fields.name: conv
fields.summary: `read`, `mut`, `ref`, `var`, `out` or `deinit` — `read` when unwritten.

fields.name: type
fields.summary: The declared type text, default value removed; empty if untyped.

fields.name: owner
fields.summary: The enclosing struct's name, or empty for a free function.

fields.name: header
fields.summary: Index of the header line in the `List[Line]`.

fields.name: body_end
fields.summary: Exclusive end of the body in the `List[Line]`.

fields.name: has_deinit
fields.summary: Defines `__deinit__` or `__del__`.

structs.name: Module
structs.summary: The functions and structs of one file.

overloads.summary: The innermost function whose body contains `line_index`.
Parameters of a `def` header line, in order.
Recover functions and structs from `lines`.

overloads.signature: def locals_of(lines: List[Line], f: Func) -> List[String]
overloads.summary: Names declared with `var` in `f`'s body, in order of declaration.

overloads.signature: def has_local(lines: List[Line], f: Func, name: String) -> Bool
def used_after(lines: List[Line], f: Func, line_index: Int, name: String) -> Bool
overloads.summary: Is `name` mentioned on any line of `f` after `line_index`?

modules.summary: Logical lines: Mojo source with comments removed, string contents blanked, and bracketed continuations joined.
modules.description:
This is all the "parsing" `mojolint` does. A rule sees a `Line` — one
statement or header, its first physical line number, its indent, the code
text, and the identifier words in it — and matches on text. No AST, no
types, no dataflow. That ceiling is deliberate; see the README.

fields.name: lineno
fields.summary: 1-based number of the first physical line.

fields.name: indent
fields.summary: Leading spaces of the first physical line.

fields.name: code
fields.summary: The text, comments stripped, every string literal reduced to `""`.

fields.name: words
fields.summary: Identifier tokens of `code`, in order.

fields.name: allow
fields.summary: Rule ids named in a `# lint: allow(...)` comment on or just above it.

fields.name: starts
fields.summary: Offset in `code` where each physical line begins; `starts[0]` is 0.

fields.name: indents
fields.summary: Leading spaces of each physical line, parallel to `starts`.

overloads.signature: def locate(self, at: Int) -> Tuple[Int, Int]
overloads.summary: The 1-based physical line and 1-based column of offset `at` in `code`, so a finding on a bracketed continuation points into the physical line it sits on.

overloads.signature: def handed_whole(code: String, name: String) -> Bool
overloads.summary: Does `code` pass the local `name` as a whole value somewhere?
overloads.description:
True when an occurrence of `name` is followed by `)` or `,` (an argument)
or `.` (a method call on it). False when it is only read *through*: as
the base of `name[...]`, or not present at all. `Ctx.to(totals)` hands
`totals`; `Int(cells[unsafe_offset=2])` merely reads a cell of `cells`.

overloads.summary: The identifier tokens of `code`, in order.
overloads.description:
Numbers are skipped, so `1_000` never becomes a word; string contents are
already gone by the time this runs.

overloads.summary: Split `source` into logical lines.
overloads.description:
Comments are removed first, then string literals are blanked, then
physical lines are joined while brackets are open. Blank lines are
dropped. A `# lint: allow(...)` comment on a line applies to that line;
on a line of its own it applies to the next code line.
